name: Ahilud
overview: Ahilud is a male biblical figure noted primarily as the father of Baana, mentioned in 1 Kings 4:12. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details in Scripture. His mention is brief but establishes a familial connection relevant to the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahilud means '[my] brother is born,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This meaning is provided in the context of 1 Kings 4:12 and does not indicate divine bestowal but serves as a personal identifier.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ahilud as the father of Baana, as inferred from 1 Kings 4:12. Beyond this relationship, no other familial connections or relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Ahilud's significance lies in his role as the progenitor of Baana, who is mentioned in the administration of King Solomon's kingdom. Though Ahilud himself is not a prominent figure, his mention helps trace the lineage and officials serving during Solomon's reign, contributing to the historical and genealogical context of the biblical record.
